_slice: Alberta energy royalties and price benchmarks
_note: Alberta's royalty system is not one formula but two parallel chains that meet only in the budget. Conventional oil and gas run on prices the province itself manufactures: the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission sets monthly oil par prices and the Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price as netbacks to the wellhead, and the Modernized Royalty Framework writes its post-C* rate tables directly in those numbers ($/m3 brackets for oil, $/GJ brackets for gas). Oil sands runs on a price Alberta has no hand in at all: the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 makes the royalty rate an explicit linear function of the NYMEX prompt-month WTI futures settlement price converted at the Bank of Canada's daily USD/CAD rate — a Chicago exchange and a federal central bank jointly determine the largest line in Alberta's revenue. The interesting shape here is how much of the chain terminates in privately published commercial price assessments (WCS-WTI broker indices, Argus Mexico Maya, ICE Brent, AECO) that are named in Alberta regulations but are not public statistical releases; those became dropped edges. The chain also runs sideways into property tax: the same Alberta Energy Regulator well records that underpin the sector feed the Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines field by field, so a well's assessed value is literally read out of AER General Well File record types.

reports.title: Oil Par Prices
reports.publisher: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission
reports.description: Monthly par prices for the four density categories of conventional Alberta crude oil (light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy), plus par prices for pentanes plus, butanes, propane and ethane. Set by the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission to represent arm's-length netback market prices at the producing battery, and published in numbered Alberta Energy Information Letters. These are the prices the conventional oil royalty formulas are written in terms of.
reports.cadence_note: Published as a numbered Information Letter roughly six weeks after the production month.

reports.title: Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price
reports.publisher: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission
reports.description: The monthly representative market price ($/GJ) for natural gas bought and sold within Alberta, calculated by the APMC on a simplified netback model. Published alongside monthly reference prices for methane, ethane, propane, butanes, pentanes plus and sulphur. The reference price is the input that values the Crown's natural gas royalty volume, and the budget forecasts it by name.
reports.cadence_note: Continuous monthly series from 1994; average market prices published for 1988-1993 on the same page.

entries.covers: June 2026 monthly reference price added to table
July 2026 monthly reference price added to table

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated-rule found on alberta.ca. The page (open.alberta.ca/opendata metadata confirms 'Monthly' maintenance/update frequency) is updated monthly with a new month's reference price. As of the page's last-modified timestamp (2026-07-15), the table showed data through May 2026 - an observed lag of roughly 6 weeks after month-end before that month's value is posted. Applying that same observed lag going forward implies June 2026 data should appear around mid-August 2026 and July 2026 data around mid-September 2026. This is an inferred pattern, not a stated publication rule.

reports.title: Alberta Modernized Royalty Framework Guidelines: Principles and Procedures
reports.description: The operating manual for the Modernized Royalty Framework governing wells drilled on or after 1 January 2017 under the Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 and the Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017. Sets out the Drilling and Completion Cost Allowance (C*), the 5% flat royalty until cumulative revenue reaches C*, and the post-C* royalty rate as a price component (rp) plus a quantity component (rq), with worked examples and rate-bracket tables keyed to par and reference prices for each hydrocarbon.
reports.cadence_note: Reissued when the framework, its rate formulas or its programs change rather than on a fixed calendar.

reports.title: Oil Sands Monthly Royalty Rates Information
reports.description: The monthly determination of oil sands royalty rates under the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009: the pre-payout gross revenue royalty percentage, the post-payout gross revenue royalty percentage and the post-payout net royalty percentage factor. Each release also publishes the WTI price and exchange rate used. Alberta Energy posts the percentages by the fifth business day following the production month.

reports.title: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (BVM) Components and Floor Price
reports.description: Monthly publication of the component values and the Floor Price used to compute a deemed bitumen value under the Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation. Operators whose bitumen is not sold at arm's length must value it at the BVM price rather than a sales price, so this release fixes the gross revenue on which oil sands royalty is charged. Accompanied by a downloadable BVM model calculator.

reports.title: NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) Futures Daily Settlement Prices
reports.description: The daily settlement price of the prompt-month West Texas Intermediate light sweet crude oil futures contract traded on NYMEX, published each trading day by CME Group. Named by Alberta regulation as the single price series that sets oil sands royalty rates and the bitumen floor price, which makes a commodity exchange's daily settlement the largest single driver of Alberta's provincial revenue.
reports.cadence_note: One settlement per exchange trading day; roughly 252 per year. Alberta averages the daily settlements over a month.

release_schedule.rule: Daily settlement prices for NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) futures are determined every trading day, based on trading activity during the settlement period of 14:28:00 to 14:30:00 Eastern Time (14:00:00-14:30:00 ET on front-month expiration day), per the NYMEX Energy Futures Daily Settlement Procedure.

entries.covers: Daily settlement price for the 2026-08-11 trading session

release_schedule.note: This is a continuous daily release published after the close of every CME/NYMEX trading day (the exchange trades Sunday evening through Friday afternoon ET, closed on exchange holidays), not a single dated 'next release' in the usual sense. 2026-08-11 is an ordinary trading day (Tuesday, no US/CME holiday), so it is the next (in-progress or upcoming) settlement date; the pattern then repeats each subsequent trading day. The corpus's releases_per_year of 252 is consistent with one settlement per NYMEX trading day per year.

reports.title: Bank of Canada Daily Exchange Rates
reports.description: The Bank of Canada's daily indicative exchange rates, published each business day at 16:30 ET. Alberta's oil sands royalty regulation and its bitumen valuation regulation both name the Bank of Canada's daily USD/CAD rate as the conversion that turns a US-dollar crude price into the Canadian-dollar price the royalty formulas run on, and both contain fallback clauses in case the Bank stops publishing it.
reports.cadence_note: Every business day; the regulations still say 'noon' rate, a series the Bank replaced in 2017 with a single daily rate.

release_schedule.rule: The daily average exchange rates are published once each business day by 16:30 ET.
release_schedule.note: This is a daily recurring release on every business day (Mon-Fri, excluding Bank of Canada holidays), published by 16:30 ET, not an annual/periodic report with a small number of releases_per_year. The entry above is the next expected business-day release (today); no fixed multi-date calendar is posted since it is effectively continuous. releases_per_year=250 on file is consistent with roughly one release per business day (~250-252 business days/year) and appears reasonable, though not explicitly stated by the publisher as a count.

reports.title: AER General Well Data Report (General Well File)
reports.description: The Alberta Energy Regulator's authoritative record of every oil, gas, oil sands and water well licensed in Alberta, updated daily and distributed as fixed-format record types carrying licence number, well status, total depth, shoe set depth, plug intervals, material and operating pressure. It is the master register the province's regulated well and pipeline assessment reads from.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously maintained and updated daily; assessment freezes it at October 31 of the assessment year.

entries.covers: Next daily update of the General Well Data Report

release_schedule.rule: The AER General Well Data Report "is updated daily and includes basic drilling data for each oil, gas, oil sands, and water well in Alberta, including domestic water wells."
release_schedule.note: This is a continuously/daily-updated dataset rather than a periodic dated release, consistent with the corpus's existing releases_per_year=365 value. There is no single 'next release' in the traditional sense - the file is refreshed every day, so the entry above simply reflects the next daily refresh from today's date (2026-08-11).

reports.title: ICE Brent Crude Futures Daily Settlement Prices
reports.description: The daily settlement price of the prompt-month Brent crude futures contract on ICE. Named verbatim in Alberta's Bitumen Valuation Methodology regulation, where the gap between Brent and WTI enters the monthly Floor Price directly. A commercial exchange's settlement price, written into provincial law as a term in a royalty formula.
reports.cadence_note: One settlement per exchange trading day; roughly 252 a year. Alberta averages the daily settlements over a month.

reports.title: Argus Mexico Maya Spot Price, FOB US Gulf Coast
reports.description: Argus Media's daily price assessment for Mexican Maya heavy crude delivered FOB at the US Gulf Coast. Alberta's bitumen valuation regulation names Argus as the publisher by company name and uses the assessment as the MMSP term in the Floor Price formula, so a proprietary heavy-crude assessment sets the floor under the province's bitumen royalty base.
reports.cadence_note: Assessed each trading day and averaged monthly for the BVM calculation. The assessment is paywalled; only the regulation naming it is public.

dependencies.basis: The MRF Guidelines state that Alberta Energy determines a well's monthly revenue by 'multiplying volumes of all the hydrocarbons produced, including test production, by their respective par/reference prices as published in the Information Letters available on the Alberta Energy website' (Revenue = Production * Par Price), and that 'the price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density'. The rate brackets are literal par-price thresholds: PP <= 251.70, 251.70 < PP <= 409.02, 409.02 < PP <= 723.64, 723.64 < PP. The Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 s.5 gives the Minister the power to 'determine an amount per cubic metre as the par price' for light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy oil, and its Schedule sets rp% = [(par price - 251.70) x ...].

Under MRF the post-C* royalty rate is rp% + rq%, where 'the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon'. C* is drawn down each month by revenue 'valued using the respective hydrocarbon par/reference price', and the gas rate tables in the guidelines are indexed on the monthly reference price in $/GJ. The Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017 correspondingly requires the Minister to prescribe a Gas Reference Price 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month along with the methane, ethane, propane, butanes and pentanes plus ISC reference prices.

reference_period.stated_as: Gas Reference Price prescribed 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month; C* is drawn down each month at that month's reference price.

dependencies.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 (AR 223/2008) s.29 sets the gross royalty rate as RG% = 1% + [FG (A - B)], where FG is '8% divided by $65 per barrel', A is 'the lesser of the WTI price for the given month ... and $120 per barrel' and B is 'the lesser of A for the month and $55 per barrel'. s.29(3)(a) defines the monthly WTI price as 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month, excluding any days where the trading price was at or below $0 per barrel', and s.29(4)(a) defines the daily WTI price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. The same A term drives the post-payout net royalty percentage factor, NRPF = 25% + (FN (A - B)).

reference_period.stated_as: 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month' — Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 s.29(3)(a).

dependencies.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 s.29(3) makes the Canadian-dollar WTI price 'the product of' the average US-dollar NYMEX settlement price and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for that month'. s.29(4)(c) specifies that 'the actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rate for a day is that published in relation to that day by the Bank of Canada', and s.29(7) provides a substitution mechanism 'if the Bank of Canada no longer publishes' it.

Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(g) provides that 'the WTI price for a month shall be the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the current month expressed in U.S. dollars', where a daily WTI price is 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. That WTI term enters the monthly Floor Price directly: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A, where A is the greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI).

reference_period.stated_as: 'the WTI price for a month shall be the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the current month' — BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(g).

dependencies.basis: BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(5) requires the Mexico Maya spot price, the Brent price, the WTI price, the synbit premium and the BVM Dilbit Value all to be 'converted from U.S. dollars per barrel to Canadian dollars per m3' using a conversion factor of 6.29234 barrels per m3 and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for the month published by the Bank of Canada, rounded to 5 decimal places'.

The Economic Outlook chapter forecasts the WTI benchmark by name in its Fiscal Year Assumptions table and treats it as the driver of the fiscal position: 'The West Texas Intermediate oil price is expected to average US$60.50 per barrel', with the differential to WCS at Hardisty forecast separately from US$11.20/bbl in 2025-26 to US$14.30/bbl by 2028-29. The revenue chapter attributes the $3.1 billion fall in non-renewable resource revenue to 'a combination of lower WTI prices and a wider light-heavy differential', and the budget notes a US$1/bbl move in the differential is worth roughly $670 million.

The Fiscal Plan's Fiscal Year Assumptions table carries an 'Alberta Reference Price (Cdn$/GJ)' row beside WTI and WCS, and the footnote to that table states that 'The Alberta Reference Price (used in natural gas royalty calculations) represents the average field price of all Alberta gas sales which normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark.' The revenue chapter then forecasts natural gas and by-product royalties off that assumption — the ARP is forecast at C$3.00/GJ in 2026-27, up from C$1.70/GJ in 2025-26, with royalties rising from $0.7 billion to $0.9 billion.

The Fiscal Plan reports the in-year revision against the same energy price assumptions the Economic Outlook set at budget: non-renewable resource revenue is 'a $0.8 billion decrease from budget', because 'The West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price is expected to average US$61.50 per barrel (/bbl) in 2025-26, a US$6.50/bbl decrease from the Budget 2025 estimate' and 'the light-heavy differential is expected to average US$11.20/bbl for 2025-26, US$5.90/bbl narrower than budgeted'. The in-year statements exist to restate revenue against a revised version of the budget's price forecast.

The 2025 Alberta Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines define 'AER means the Alberta Energy Regulator' and then read assessment inputs straight out of its records: for pipelines and wells licensed by the AER 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'. Pipeline assessment classification codes are set by 'pipeline material, outside diameter, and the maximum operating pressure ... as contained in the records of the AER', and well depth is taken field by field — 'Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)', 'Deepest shoe set depth (field SHOE-SET-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 040)', plug tops from record type 055. The guidelines also rely on the AER Insolvency List.

reference_period.stated_as: 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'.

dependencies.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(f) defines the Brent price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of the Brent crude futures as traded on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)'. That term enters the monthly Floor Price through A = greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI), alongside the WTI term already recorded. Promoted from _dropped in V0.5 under the commercial-source decision: the evidence is exactly as strong as the WTI edge and was only ever held back because ICE is a commercial exchange.

reference_period.stated_as: Daily ICE prompt-month Brent settlements entering the monthly Floor Price determination under BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(f).

dependencies.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(e) states that 'the daily Mexico Maya Spot Price FOB at the U.S. Gulf Coast shall be as published by Argus Media Inc.' The MMSP is the leading term in the Floor Price: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A. Alberta legislation names a private price-reporting agency by company name, which is as explicit as evidence gets.

reference_period.stated_as: Daily Argus Mexico Maya assessments entering the monthly Floor Price determination under BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(e).

dependencies.basis: Real but undocumented as a formula. The APMC describes par prices as 'provincial arm's length netback market prices at the producing battery' derived from actual arm's-length sales, and Alberta light crude tracks WTI closely enough that the relationship is not in doubt. No Alberta document sets out a par-price formula in terms of a named benchmark, so a documented edge would be inference dressed as arithmetic.

Designated industrial property assessment values wells and pipelines on regulated cost-and-depreciation schedules, and the facilities being assessed are the same oil sands operations whose output the royalty regime measures. The connection is real at the level of subject matter but no document ties the DIP requisition to the royalty determination as an input.

_dropped.why: The Budget 2026 Fiscal Plan says the Alberta Reference Price 'normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark' (AECO), which is suggestive, but 'normally follows' is a correlation statement, not a calculation. The APMC's 'simplified netback model' inputs are not published as a formula, and AECO itself is a commercial index (ICE NGX) rather than an official statistical release, so it does not qualify as a graph node.

_dropped.edge: ab-bvm-components -> WCS-WTI broker index / CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values
_dropped.why: BVM Regulation s.1(3)(c) sets the WCS index as 'the weighted average, based on trading volumes, of the "WCS-WTI" index published for that month by the commodity brokers specified', and s.1(3)(d) takes the Condensate Allowance Price and CRW density from 'the Equalization Steering Committee and as published on the website of the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers'. Both are named in law but neither is a stable, identifiable public release; the broker list is even set by ministerial order.

_dropped.edge: ab-oilsands-royalty-rates -> AER ST3 / ST98 production statistics
_dropped.why: Intuitive but wrong in direction of causation. Royalty is computed from operator volumetric submissions through Petrinex, not from the AER's published statistical series; ST3 and ST98 are downstream summaries of the same raw volumes. No royalty document names an AER statistical report as an input.

The budget forecasts 'WCS @ Hardisty (Cdn$/bbl)' as a named assumption row, but the WCS assessment is produced by commercial brokers and price reporting agencies with no official publisher, so there is no report node to point at. The WTI edge captures the same relationship at the point where an identifiable publisher exists.

_dropped.edge: ab-bvm-components -> WCS-WTI broker index / CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values
_dropped.why: Still out after the V0.5 commercial-source decision, and for a different reason than ICE and Argus were. Those two failed the old officialness rule and the rule bent. This one fails identifiability, which no rule change fixes: BVM Regulation s.1(3)(c) sets the WCS index from 'the commodity brokers specified' in a list the Minister sets by order, so there is no stable publication to point a node at, and the CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values in s.1(3)(d) are committee outputs rather than a recurring release. A node needs a real, named, recurring publication; commercial is now allowed, unidentifiable is not.

_status: SWEPT 2026-08-09 (dropped-sweep, long tail): all 5 _dropped entries read in full. All correctly reasoned: WCS/AECO/broker-set commodity indices are not official statistical releases (unpublishable-source, consistent with the V0.5 commercial-source rule's identifiability requirement), and the royalty-direction entry correctly identifies Petrinex submissions, not AER statistics, as the real input. No reports or dependencies changed.
